Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
# Summary of the 1997 Conservative Party Manifesto

## Overview
The 1997 Conservative Party Manifesto, titled "You Can Only Be Sure with the Conservatives," presented a vision for Britain under continued Conservative leadership following 18 years in power. The document emphasized maintaining economic success, promoting individual ownership, and resisting European federalism.

## Economic Achievements and Goals
The manifesto highlighted Britain's economic transformation since 1979, including record low unemployment, inflation below 4% for over four years, and the lowest mortgage rates in 30 years. The Conservatives pledged to maintain tight public spending controls, aiming to reduce the basic income tax rate to 20p and keep Britain as Europe's lowest-tax major economy.

## Employment and Enterprise
Central to the manifesto was job creation through enterprise rather than government intervention. The document strongly opposed the European Social Chapter and national minimum wage, arguing these would destroy jobs by burdening businesses. The party promoted small business growth through reduced corporation tax, simplified regulations, and reformed business rates.

## Families and Ownership
The Conservatives proposed expanding a "property-owning democracy" through continued home ownership programs, employee share schemes, and pension reforms. A revolutionary proposal would provide all young workers with personal pension funds through national insurance rebates. Tax reforms would allow one-earner families to transfer unused personal allowances to working spouses.

## Education
The manifesto promised an "Education Guarantee" with national performance targets, published school results, and intervention in failing schools. It promoted school diversity through grammar schools, specialist schools, and expanded grant-maintained schools while maintaining nursery vouchers for all four-year-olds.

## Healthcare
The NHS received strong commitments for continued real-terms funding increases. Reforms focused on expanding GP services, reducing waiting times, and encouraging private sector investment through the Private Finance Initiative while maintaining free healthcare based on clinical need.

## Law and Order
The Conservatives took credit for four consecutive years of falling crime and promised continued investment in policing, CCTV expansion, and tough sentencing. Mandatory minimum sentences were proposed for persistent burglars and drug dealers. Juvenile crime would be tackled through faster court procedures and parental responsibility orders.

## Europe and Constitution
The manifesto firmly opposed a federal Europe, promising to retain Britain's veto and Social Chapter opt-out. On the single currency, it maintained a "wait and see" position with a referendum guarantee. The party strongly opposed devolution to Scotland and Wales, warning it would threaten the Union.

## Defence and Foreign Policy
Britain's global role was emphasized through NATO membership, UN Security Council participation, and Commonwealth ties. The manifesto committed to maintaining professional armed forces and the nuclear deterrent while adapting to post-Cold War realities.

## Conclusion
The document presented a choice between continued Conservative success and what it characterized as risky Labour alternatives, concluding with 25 specific pledges covering taxation, public services, law and order, and national sovereignty.
</text>
